questions.stem: A psychologist designed and conducted a study to determine whether playing a certain educational game increases middle school students' accuracy in adding fractions. For the study, the psychologist chose a random sample of 35 students from all of the students at one of the middle schools in a large city. The psychologist found that students who played the game showed significant improvement in accuracy when adding fractions. What is the largest group to which the results of the study can be generalized?

options.A: The 35 students in the sample
options.B: All students at the school
options.C: All middle school students in the city
options.D: All students in the city

questions.stem: The members of a city council wanted to assess the opinions of all city residents about converting an open field into a dog park. The council surveyed a sample of 500 city residents who own dogs. The survey showed that the majority of those sampled were in favor of the dog park. Which of the following is true about the city council's survey?

options.A: It shows that the majority of city residents are in favor of the dog park.
options.B: The survey sample should have included more residents who are dog owners.
options.C: The survey sample should have consisted entirely of residents who do not own dogs.
options.D: The survey sample is biased because it is not representative of all city residents.

questions.stem: Near the end of a US cable news show, the host invited viewers to respond to a poll on the show's website that asked, "Do you support the new federal policy discussed during the show?" At the end of the show, the host reported that 28% responded "Yes," and 70% responded "No." Which of the following best explains why the results are unlikely to represent the sentiments of the population of the United States?

options.A: The percentages do not add up to 100%, so any possible conclusions from the poll are invalid.
options.B: Those who responded to the poll were not a random sample of the population of the United States.
options.C: There were not 50% "Yes" responses and 50% "No" responses.
options.D: The show did not allow viewers enough time to respond to the poll.

questions.stem: Researchers randomly sample 100 city voters but do not assign any treatment. What does the random sampling primarily support?

options.A: Establishing a causal effect of a treatment
options.B: Guaranteeing that every response is truthful
options.C: Eliminating all sampling variability
options.D: Generalizing the sample results to the population of city voters

questions.explanation: D is correct. Random sampling supports representativeness and population generalization.

questions.stem: Researchers recruit 110 volunteers and randomly assign them to two exercise plans. What does the random assignment primarily support?

options.A: Comparing the methods in a way that can support a causal conclusion for the participants
options.B: Generalizing automatically to every student
options.C: Guaranteeing identical outcomes
options.D: Removing the need for a control group

questions.explanation: A is correct. Random assignment balances other factors between treatment groups and supports causal inference.

questions.stem: Researchers take a random sample of 120 county households and then randomly assign the sampled participants to two reminder messages. What can the design potentially support?

options.A: Neither generalization nor causal comparison
options.B: Both population generalization and a causal comparison
options.C: Only a description of volunteers
options.D: A conclusion with no uncertainty

questions.explanation: B is correct. Random sampling supports generalization, and random assignment supports causation.
